# Md. Sabbir Hossain Molla

> Md. Sabbir Hossain Molla is a researcher in machine and deep learning for power systems, focusing on smart grids, digital twins, and renewable energy. He holds a BSc in Electrical, Electronic and Communication Engineering (EECE) from the Military Institute of Science and Technology (MIST), Dhaka, Bangladesh, and is a Research Assistant at the Smart Grid & Sustainable Energy Transition Lab (SET Lab), Department of EECE, MIST, working on an AI-enabled digital twin of a solar PV plant (SolarDT, funded by BEPRC). He is a prospective MS/PhD applicant.

This is his official academic website. Research interests: machine learning, digital twins, power systems, smart grids, renewable energy, electricity theft detection, solar PV forecasting, and power electronics.

## Publications

- [A Target-Augmented Residual BiGRU Model for Ultra-Short-Term PV Output Power Forecasting](https://mshmolla.github.io/publications#bigru-pv-forecasting): accepted at IEEE SUSTAIN 2026
- [Regime-Aware Soft-Probabilistic GMM Integrated Ensemble Learning Framework for Solar PV Power Forecasting](https://mshmolla.github.io/publications#gmm-pv-forecasting): accepted at IEEE SUSTAIN 2026
- [Machine Learning and Explainable AI for Robust Smart Grid Security: A New Dataset Study](https://doi.org/10.1109/QPAIN69676.2026.11545639): IEEE QPAIN 2026
- [An Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Dysarthria Detection Using Deep Acoustic Embeddings and Prosodic Cues](https://doi.org/10.1109/QPAIN69676.2026.11546156): IEEE QPAIN 2026
- [SecureGrid: A Robust Voting Ensemble Model for Non-Technical Loss (NTL) Detection in Smart Meter Data](https://doi.org/10.1109/COMPAS67506.2025.11381615): IEEE COMPAS 2025
- [Generalising Violence Detection with a New Near-Real-World Violence Dataset](https://doi.org/10.1109/ICAEEE62219.2024.10561682): IEEE ICAEEE 2024
- [Enhanced Detection of Electricity Theft in Smart Grids Using a Machine Learning Boosting Classifiers Based Voting Ensemble Model](https://doi.org/10.13140/RG.2.2.23095.89767): BSc thesis, MIST, 2024
